**1. Evan Huang (Frontend Developer & Studio Founder)**
Evan Huang is a former Frontend Developer with significant experience in React, Next.js, and TypeScript. He is currently focusing on his studies but remains passionate about coding and problem-solving. He founded Tech-Art Studio, a community-driven web development studio that focuses on high-quality websites and custom digital solutions, encouraging collaboration from developers of all skill levels. His featured projects include "One Calendar," a privacy-first calendar web app with modern security features, and a Resend email sending web application named "Mail," both built with Next.js, React, and TypeScript. He also maintains a personal portfolio using Next.js, React, TailwindCSS, and TypeScript. **2. Evan Huang (Full Stack Data Scientist)**

**3. Evan Huang (Distributed Systems & Developer Tooling Specialist)**
An Evan Huang with a GitHub presence (evanqhuang) focuses on distributed systems, developer tooling, and even underwater hardware. His projects include "HostelHound," which provides full-service price history and predictions for hostels using SvelteKit, Rust, and TimescaleDB, and "Camazotz," a project involving the design and sale of cave diving equipment, including firmware for a handheld underwater cave-mapping device written in C. He also developed "FinFeed," a live fish-tank camera streaming to any browser, and "geo-daemon," a weekly tracker for brand visibility across AI search engines using TypeScript. His technical stack includes Go, TypeScript, Python, Rust, React, and Svelte.

While primarily an inventor, Evan Huang, a Year 12 student, developed "DrinkBot," a robot designed to assist the elderly and disabled by grabbing and delivering cups. He is recognized as a RISE Global Winner and VEX Robotics Challenge World Winner, motivated by a personal mission to improve the quality of life for the elderly and disabled through technology.

Software engineer Evan Huang has built an extensive portfolio spanning embedded hardware, developer tools, web apps, and distributed systems, while other individuals with the same name are known for ventures in healthcare technology, real estate, and hospitality.
Evan Huang (Software Engineer & Hardware Maker)
According to his portfolio on evanqhuang.com , he is a Capital One software engineer and independent maker who has built the following projects:
Ixchel. A handheld cave-survey device featuring custom hardware, dual-core RP2350 firmware, a live stick map, and post-dive 3D visualization.
Maxwell's Razor. A largely 3D-printed toolchanger built for the Hypercube EVO 3D printer using mechanical coupling, magnetic clamping, and Klipper macros.
HostelHound. A web platform built with Rust, SvelteKit, and Postgres that tracks prices across 15,000+ hostels in nearly 800 cities, complete with price forecasts, a trip planner, and a ChatGPT connector.
UnFare. A flight-price monitor using Python, FastAPI, and statistical modeling to flag unusually low airfares against airline-specific baselines.
Pi Notes. A TypeScript extension designed to preserve coding-agent task state across context compaction and session branches.
Recadero & crumb. Go CLI developer tools created at Capital One—Recadero generates event contracts across production services to eliminate schema drift, while crumb connects Jira, GitHub, and git history to link requirements with code and tests.
Camazotz Diving. An e-commerce storefront for his cave-diving gear company featuring interactive 3D color configuration and Stripe checkout.
Polarwrapped. A React and Mapbox web app that turns Polarsteps travel data into animated year-in-review recaps.
HashTop. A cryptocurrency mining platform he founded and operated (2020–2023) with distributed services for GPU telemetry and remote node management.
FinFeed. A live fish-tank camera streamed from a Raspberry Pi via Twitch using hardware video encoding.

Healthcare Tech (CareSignal & Epharmix). Co-founder and Chief Developer of CareSignal (formerly Epharmix), a deviceless remote patient monitoring platform that uses automated text messages and phone calls to track chronic conditions.
Hospitality & Real Estate (Baohaus & Batu Capital). Co-founder of the New York and Los Angeles restaurant Baohaus, co-founder of the investment firm Batu Capital , and leader of The Huang Team at Charney Companies (inspiration for Fresh Off the Boat).
Assistive Robotics (DrinkBot). Student engineer and RISE Global Winner who invented , an assistive robotics device built to help elderly and disabled individuals drink independently.

Evan Huang's underwater cave mapping project is called Camazotz. This project focuses on designing and selling specialized cave diving equipment, including a handheld device for real-time underwater cave mapping.

The core of this project involves the "camazotz-ixchel" component, which is RP2350 firmware. This firmware enables the handheld device to create live "stick maps" by integrating data from an encoder, an Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU), and a depth sensor. This fusion of sensor data allows for real-time navigation and mapping within underwater cave environments.

El proyecto de mapeo de cuevas submarinas de Evan Huang es Ixchel (desarrollado bajo su proyecto Camazotz), un dispositivo portátil de topografía submarina diseñado para automatizar el levantamiento de mapas durante inmersiones en cuevas.
Características principales
Automatización de mediciones: Sustituye o agiliza el registro manual tradicional midiendo continuamente la distancia (mediante la rotación de un carrete de línea / encoder ), la orientación o rumbo (mediante un IMU) y la profundidad.
Visualización en tiempo real y posterior: Genera un mapa de líneas (live stick map) en tiempo real durante la inmersión y permite crear visualizaciones en 3D después de bucear.
Hardware y firmware: Utiliza hardware personalizado, diseño mecánico en Fusion360/impresión 3D y firmware en C/C++ para el microcontrolador de doble núcleo RP2350 con fusión de sensores.
Puedes revisar los detalles técnicos del dispositivo en y el código del firmware en GitHub - evanqhuang/camazotz-ixchel .
Si te interesa profundizar, dime si buscas detalles sobre el funcionamiento de los sensores , la arquitectura del firmware RP2350 o el contexto de topografía en buceo en cuevas .

Several individuals and projects are actively building DIY (Do-It-Yourself) hardware for underwater cave mapping, often leveraging open-source components and software to create more affordable and accessible solutions.

Notable efforts include:

*   **9nl** has developed a DIY sensor system specifically for 3D cave mapping. This system utilizes a handheld Velodyne VLP 16 lidar unit, a Raspberry Pi 5, and an Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) to perform Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) in underground environments where traditional navigation systems like GPS are ineffective.
*   **Phil Underwood** has been a pioneer in open-source cave surveying hardware, evolving his designs over several generations. His most recent iteration incorporates a Raspberry Pi 5 Compute Module and two low-light cameras, enabling the creation of textured 3D models of caves through photogrammetry.
*   **Addison Snyder**, affiliated with Free Springs LLC, is also working on a self-contained LiDAR setup specifically designed for use in underwater caves.
*   **Richard Wylde, Fred Devos, and their colleagues** are involved in mapping subterranean cenote networks. They enhance the accuracy of their acoustic and magnetic mapping efforts by utilizing Raspberry Shake, a Raspberry Pi-based seismograph.
*   **Jason Bula** is recognized for originating DIY static laser scanners for cave mapping, using a Velodyne VLP16 and MATLAB-based code.
*   **Tim Hansen and Andreas Birk** from Constructor University have contributed an open-source software framework for real-time underwater mapping. Their system is designed to work with low-cost marine robotics components, such as the BlueRobotics BlueROV2, a Ping360 Mechanical Scanning Sonar, and an A50 Doppler Velocity Log, all powered by a Raspberry Pi 4.

While not exclusively for *cave* mapping, **The Open Sonar Project (OSP)**, initially a senior design project at the University of New Brunswick, is an entirely open-source initiative focused on hydrographic surveying. It provides a platform for building low-cost, open-source single-beam sonar systems and uncrewed surface vessels for ocean mapping, offering valuable insights and components for broader DIY underwater mapping applications. Similarly, **Alex Williams** designed an open-source underwater glider that **Jeremy Granadillo** later revised for reef mapping, demonstrating a broader trend in DIY underwater robotics for data collection.

Independent makers, researchers, and cave divers are building DIY and custom hardware for underwater cave mapping—including LiDAR/SLAM rigs, open-source laser surveying tools, and low-cost action-camera photogrammetry/SLAM setups.
Notable Builders & Projects
Addison Snyder (Free Springs): Developing a self-contained underwater LiDAR/SLAM cave mapper and mapping springs in Florida, as shared on the Blue Robotics Forums .
Open-Source CircuitPython Cave Surveyor: Featured on element14, this DIY tool uses a Xiao nRF52840 Sense module, CircuitPython, a laser rangefinder, and a 3D-printed/greased enclosure designed for easy user modification and community pull requests.
DIY 360° LiDAR & SLAM Builders: Independent creators on YouTube and Instagram (such as @piedro_79 and DIY LiDAR makers) have shared custom 3D-printed rotating LiDAR scanners, deskewing scripts for point clouds, and multi-sensor SLAM builds tested in caves .
Academic & Low-Cost Camera SLAM Researchers: Researchers studying underwater cave segments—such as those behind the Devil's Eye System paper—have built frameworks using inexpensive action cameras and dive computers for visual-inertial SLAM and Structure-from-Motion (SfM) reconstruction.
(Note: Alongside DIY builds, divers also use specialized surveyor-created tools like Sebastien Kister's mNemo line-rolling survey device paired with Ariane Line software, as well as commercial/custom AUVs and sonar/ENC gear.)

results.response_text:
The Camazotz Cave Mapping Project refers to the "Cave Mapper System," an advanced, custom-built underwater cave mapping solution developed by Camazotz Diving. The primary goal of this project is to transform exploration dives into detailed 3D maps in real time.

The system integrates multiple sensor inputs to construct a real-time model of the cave passage as a diver swims. Key components include:
*   **Depth sensor:** A high-precision pressure transducer for accurate depth profiling.
*   **Distance measurement:** A magnetic encoder coupled to a wheel that tracks the deployment of a line.
*   **Compass/IMU:** A 9-axis inertial measurement unit for determining heading and attitude.
*   **Data logger:** Records all sensor data for subsequent post-dive processing.

A dual-core processor within the system combines this sensor data rapidly to plot the diver's position, resulting in a real-time "stick map" of the path through the cave. After a dive, the collected data can be processed using Camazotz's software to generate 2D passage profiles (plan and cross-section views), 3D point cloud visualizations, and export to standard cave survey formats like Compass and Walls. Camazotz Diving also offers free, browser-based cave mapping software for visualizing 3D cave surveys. The Cave Mapper System is actively under development and undergoing field testing.

Camazotz and Ixchel are both significant deities within Maya mythology, rather than entities that were "built" by someone. There is no mythological account or historical record suggesting that one constructed the other.

Camazotz is known as the Maya god of bats, often referred to as a "death bat" in the K'iche' language. He is associated with night, death, and sacrifice, and is a notable figure in the Popol Vuh, the sacred text of the K'iche' Maya. In these narratives, Camazotz is depicted as a bat-like spirit or a group of deadly bat beings encountered by the Hero Twins, Hunahpu and Xbalanque, during their trials in the underworld of Xibalba.

Ixchel, on the other hand, is the Maya goddess of love, marriage, beauty, pregnancy, healing, medicine, the moon, land, and water. She is also known as the divine mother and is often depicted as the wife of the god Itzamna.

While both are part of the complex pantheon of Mayan gods and goddesses, and some fictional works or broader mythological contexts might mention their interactions or shared pantheon, there is no information in the available records to indicate that Camazotz "built" Ixchel or vice versa. They exist as distinct, powerful entities within Mayan cosmology.
